Job T01: usp_load_dim_customer (tsql), file estate/tsql/T01_usp_load_dim_customer.sql.
Customer dimension, one row per CRM customer.

Code:
  1 | /*==============================================================================
  2 |   Job      : dw.usp_load_dim_customer
  3 |   Purpose  : Customer dimension for the marketing and pricing teams. One row
  4 |              per CRM customer with the customer's current details from the
  5 |              CRM extract, plus sales region, Eircode check, initials and
  6 |              segment flags for campaigns and the pricing models.
  7 |   Output   : dw.dim_customer (truncated and reloaded on every run)
  8 |   Author   : DOC
  9 | 
 10 |   Change log
 11 |     2013-05-20  DOC   Initial version
 12 |     2014-11-03  DOC   Sales region from county for the regional reports (CR-0412)
 13 |     2015-01-26  DOC   full_name and initials for the mail merge (CR-0538)
 14 |     2016-02-18  AMcG  Eircode added, with a format check (CR-0877)
 15 |     2017-09-07  AMcG  email_shared_count for the marketing duplicate review
 16 |                       (CR-1190)
 17 |     2018-05-21  AMcG  Opt-in defaults to N when the customer was never asked
 18 |                       (GDPR, CR-1342)
 19 |     2019-03-25  SR    age_at_join for the pricing models (CR-1564)
 20 |     2019-11-04  KB    CRM extract is now change data capture: one row per
 21 |                       saved version, keep the current one (CR-1702)
 22 |     2020-10-12  SR    is_standard_segment for the renewal campaign (CR-1841)
 23 |     2021-06-14  KB    Logging through etl.usp_log_step (CR-2003)
 24 | ==============================================================================*/
 25 | SET NOCOUNT ON;
 26 | GO
 27 | IF OBJECT_ID(N'dw.dim_customer', N'U') IS NULL
 28 | CREATE TABLE dw.dim_customer (
 29 |     customer_id          INT            NOT NULL,
 30 |     first_name           NVARCHAR(40)   NOT NULL,
 31 |     last_name            NVARCHAR(60)   NOT NULL,
 32 |     full_name            NVARCHAR(101)  NOT NULL,
 33 |     initials             NVARCHAR(2)    NOT NULL,
 34 |     email                VARCHAR(120)   NULL,
 35 |     email_shared_count   INT            NOT NULL,
 36 |     date_of_birth        DATE           NULL,
 37 |     age_at_join          INT            NULL,
 38 |     address_line1        NVARCHAR(100)  NULL,
 39 |     town                 NVARCHAR(50)   NULL,
 40 |     county               VARCHAR(30)    NULL,
 41 |     region               VARCHAR(12)    NOT NULL,
 42 |     eircode              VARCHAR(10)    NULL,
 43 |     eircode_valid        CHAR(1)        NOT NULL,
 44 |     segment_code         CHAR(4)        NULL,
 45 |     is_standard_segment  CHAR(1)        NOT NULL,
 46 |     marketing_opt_in     CHAR(1)        NOT NULL,
 47 |     customer_since       DATE           NOT NULL,
 48 |     source_system        VARCHAR(10)    NOT NULL,
 49 |     version_count        INT            NOT NULL,
 50 |     record_updated_at    DATETIME2(0)   NOT NULL,
 51 |     as_of_date           DATE           NOT NULL,
 52 |     CONSTRAINT pk_dim_customer PRIMARY KEY CLUSTERED (customer_id)
 53 | );
 54 | GO
 55 | CREATE OR ALTER PROCEDURE dw.usp_load_dim_customer
 56 |     @AsOfDate DATE
 57 | AS
 58 | BEGIN
 59 |     SET NOCOUNT ON;
 60 | 
 61 |     DECLARE @job_name  VARCHAR(128) = 'dw.usp_load_dim_customer',
 62 |             @rows      INT,
 63 |             @err_msg   NVARCHAR(4000),
 64 |             @err_no    INT;
 65 | 
 66 |     BEGIN TRY
 67 |         EXEC etl.usp_log_step @job_name = @job_name, @step_name = 'start', @status = 'STARTED';
 68 | 
 69 |         IF OBJECT_ID('tempdb..#customer_versions') IS NOT NULL DROP TABLE #customer_versions;
 70 |         IF OBJECT_ID('tempdb..#customer') IS NOT NULL DROP TABLE #customer;
 71 | 
 72 |         /* 1. Customer versions saved up to the reporting date. The CRM extract
 73 |               writes a new row every time a record is saved. */
 74 |         SELECT  c.customer_id,
 75 |                 c.first_name,
 76 |                 c.last_name,
 77 |                 c.email,
 78 |                 c.date_of_birth,
 79 |                 c.address_line1,
 80 |                 c.town,
 81 |                 c.county,
 82 |                 c.eircode,
 83 |                 c.segment_code,
 84 |                 c.marketing_opt_in,
 85 |                 c.customer_since,
 86 |                 c.source_system,
 87 |                 c.updated_at,
 88 |                 c._row_seq,
 89 |                 COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY c.customer_id) AS version_count
 90 |         INTO    #customer_versions
 91 |         FROM    stg.customers c WITH (NOLOCK)
 92 |         WHERE   CAST(c.updated_at AS DATE) <= @AsOfDate;
 93 | 
 94 |         SET @rows = @@ROWCOUNT;
 95 |         EXEC etl.usp_log_step @job_name = @job_name, @step_name = 'customer versions', @status = 'INFO', @rows_affected = @rows;
 96 | 
 97 |         /* 2. Keep the current version of each customer */
 98 |         SELECT  v.*
 99 |         INTO    #customer
100 |         FROM   (SELECT  cv.*,
101 |                         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY cv.customer_id
102 |                                            ORDER BY cv.updated_at, cv._row_seq) AS version_no
103 |                 FROM    #customer_versions cv) v
104 |         WHERE   v.version_no = 1;
105 | 
106 |         SET @rows = @@ROWCOUNT;
107 |         EXEC etl.usp_log_step @job_name = @job_name, @step_name = 'current versions', @status = 'INFO', @rows_affected = @rows;
108 | 
109 |         /* 3. Reload the dimension */
110 |         BEGIN TRANSACTION;
111 | 
112 |         TRUNCATE TABLE dw.dim_customer;
113 | 
114 |         INSERT INTO dw.dim_customer
115 |                (customer_id, first_name, last_name, full_name, initials, email,
116 |                 email_shared_count, date_of_birth, age_at_join, address_line1, town,
117 |                 county, region, eircode, eircode_valid, segment_code, is_standard_segment,
118 |                 marketing_opt_in, customer_since, source_system, version_count,
119 |                 record_updated_at, as_of_date)
120 |         SELECT  k.customer_id,
121 |                 RTRIM(k.first_name),
122 |                 k.last_name,
123 |                 RTRIM(k.first_name) + N' ' + RTRIM(k.last_name),
124 |                 UPPER(SUBSTRING(k.first_name, 0, 2) + SUBSTRING(k.last_name, 0, 2)),
125 |                 k.email,
126 |                 CASE WHEN k.email IS NULL THEN 0
127 |                      ELSE COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY k.email) END,
128 |                 k.date_of_birth,
129 |                 DATEDIFF(YEAR, k.date_of_birth, k.customer_since),
130 |                 k.address_line1,
131 |                 k.town,
132 |                 k.county,
133 |                 -- sales regions as agreed with distribution (CR-0412)
134 |                 CASE WHEN k.county IN ('Dublin', 'Kildare', 'Meath', 'Wicklow', 'Louth', 'Wexford') THEN 'EAST'
135 |                      WHEN k.county IN ('Cork', 'Kerry', 'Limerick', 'Tipperary', 'Waterford', 'Kilkenny', 'Carlow') THEN 'SOUTH'
136 |                      WHEN k.county IN ('Galway', 'Mayo', 'Clare', 'Roscommon') THEN 'WEST'
137 |                      WHEN k.county IN ('Donegal', 'Sligo', 'Leitrim', 'Cavan', 'Monaghan') THEN 'NORTH-WEST'
138 |                      WHEN k.county IN ('Westmeath', 'Longford', 'Offaly', 'Laois') THEN 'MIDLANDS'
139 |                      ELSE 'UNKNOWN'
140 |                 END,
141 |                 k.eircode,
142 |                 -- routing key (3) and unique identifier (4), keyed with or without the space
143 |                 CASE WHEN LEN(k.eircode) = 7 THEN 'Y'
144 |                      WHEN LEN(k.eircode) = 8 AND SUBSTRING(k.eircode, 4, 1) = ' ' THEN 'Y'
145 |                      ELSE 'N'
146 |                 END,
147 |                 k.segment_code,
148 |                 CASE WHEN k.segment_code = 'STD' THEN 'Y' ELSE 'N' END,
149 |                 ISNULL(k.marketing_opt_in, 'N'),
150 |                 k.customer_since,
151 |                 UPPER(RTRIM(k.source_system)),
152 |                 k.version_count,
153 |                 k.updated_at,
154 |                 @AsOfDate
155 |         FROM    #customer k;
156 | 
157 |         SET @rows = @@ROWCOUNT;
158 | 
159 |         COMMIT TRANSACTION;
160 | 
161 |         EXEC etl.usp_log_step @job_name = @job_name, @step_name = 'dw.dim_customer', @status = 'INFO', @rows_affected = @rows;
162 |         EXEC etl.usp_log_step @job_name = @job_name, @step_name = 'end', @status = 'SUCCESS';
163 |     END TRY
164 |     BEGIN CATCH
165 |         IF @@TRANCOUNT > 0 ROLLBACK TRANSACTION;
166 | 
167 |         SELECT  @err_msg = ERROR_MESSAGE(),
168 |                 @err_no  = ERROR_NUMBER();
169 | 
170 |         EXEC etl.usp_log_step @job_name = @job_name, @step_name = 'end', @status = 'FAILED',
171 |              @message = @err_msg, @error_number = @err_no;
172 |         THROW;
173 |     END CATCH
174 | END;
175 | GO

Trap cards:
- TSQL-01 (semantic) Case-insensitive collation in =, IN, GROUP BY, DISTINCT, PARTITION BY and joins. Legacy: Under a case-insensitive collation such as SQL_Latin1_General_CP1_CI_AS, text compares equal regardless of letter case (and of trailing spaces, see TSQL-02): state = 'ACTIVE' also matches 'Active' and 'active'; GROUP BY, DISTINCT, PARTITION BY and join keys put case variants together. The stored value is returned unchanged. Spark: Spark compares strings in binary order: 'Active' <> 'ACTIVE', so a filter drops case variants, a GROUP BY splits them into separate groups and a join misses them.
- TSQL-02 (semantic) Comparisons ignore trailing spaces; CHAR(n) pads with spaces. Legacy: SQL Server pads the shorter string with spaces before comparing, so 'WEST ' = 'WEST' (also in IN, GROUP BY and joins). CHAR(n) and NCHAR(n) values are stored and returned padded to n characters: 'AB' in a CHAR(4) column is 'AB '. LEN() ignores trailing spaces (TSQL-15). Leading spaces always count. Spark: Spark compares strings exactly, so 'WEST ' <> 'WEST', and its string type never pads. A value read from a CHAR source column keeps whatever spaces it was stored with.
- TSQL-03 (semantic) Integer division truncates. Legacy: INT / INT is integer division in T-SQL, truncating toward zero: 7 / 2 = 3, -7 / 2 = -3. The result type follows the operands, so the fraction is lost before any later cast, e.g. CAST(qty / pack_size AS DECIMAL(9,2)) or 100 * a / b. Spark: Spark's / always returns a double (7 / 2 = 3.5); DIV is integer division.
- TSQL-04 (semantic) DATEDIFF counts boundaries crossed, not elapsed periods. Legacy: DATEDIFF(datepart, a, b) counts the datepart boundaries crossed between a and b: DATEDIFF(year, '2025-12-31', '2026-01-01') = 1 and DATEDIFF(month, '2025-01-31', '2025-02-01') = 1. DATEDIFF(week, ...) counts Sundays crossed, whatever SET DATEFIRST says. DATEDIFF(day, ...) on DATE values equals the day difference. Spark: datediff(end, start) counts days (arguments reversed); months_between returns a fraction with its own month-end rule; floor(months/12) counts elapsed years, not boundaries.
- TSQL-05 (semantic) + concatenation with NULL yields NULL. Legacy: With CONCAT_NULL_YIELDS_NULL ON (the default), 'A' + NULL is NULL, so a whole concatenation is NULL when any part is. CONCAT() and CONCAT_WS() treat NULL as empty. Spark: Spark's + is arithmetic only; concat() returns NULL when any argument is NULL, while concat_ws() skips NULLs and format_string writes 'null'.
- TSQL-06 (semantic) ISNULL takes the type of its first argument; NULL treated as equal in change checks. Legacy: ISNULL(a, b) returns a's data type, so the replacement b is converted to it: a VARCHAR(5) column with ISNULL(col, 'UNKNOWN') returns 'UNKNO' (truncated), and ISNULL(int_col, 0.5) returns 0. COALESCE uses the highest-precedence type instead. Change detection written as ISNULL(src, '') <> ISNULL(tgt, '') treats NULL and '' as the same value. Spark: coalesce() keeps the replacement as written ('UNKNOWN') and widens types; it never truncates.
- TSQL-07 (semantic) DECIMAL precision and scale, and ROUND on computed values. Legacy: DECIMAL arithmetic follows fixed precision and scale rules (e.g. division keeps at least 6 decimal places, results are capped at 38 digits and the scale shrinks to fit); intermediate results are rounded at each step to their result type. ROUND(x, n) rounds half away from zero; ROUND(x, n, 1) truncates. Assigning to a DECIMAL(p,s) column rounds. Spark: Spark's decimal rules are similar but not identical (scale reduction, and doubles if an operand is a double literal); F.round on a double rounds the binary value, so a computed 2.675 (really 2.67499...) rounds to 2.67; bround is half-even.
- TSQL-08 (semantic) TOP and TOP WITH TIES. Legacy: TOP n returns n rows in ORDER BY order (arbitrary among ties unless the ORDER BY is unique); TOP n WITH TIES also returns every row tied with the last one. Spark: limit(n) after orderBy returns exactly n rows; ties need a rank window.
- TSQL-09 (construct) CROSS APPLY / OUTER APPLY with TOP 1. Legacy: CROSS APPLY (SELECT TOP 1 ... WHERE inner.k = outer.k ORDER BY ...) picks one inner row per outer row and drops outer rows with no match; OUTER APPLY keeps them with NULLs. Spark: Spark has no APPLY; a lateral subquery or a window replaces it.
- TSQL-10 (construct) UPDATE ... FROM. Legacy: UPDATE t SET ... FROM t JOIN s ON ... updates each target row from one matching source row; with several matches, which one wins is undefined. Spark: DataFrames are immutable; an update becomes a join plus a select.
- TSQL-11 (construct) MERGE and type-2 history. Legacy: MERGE matches target and source rows and updates, inserts or deletes in one statement. Type-2 history closes the current version (valid_to, is_current) of changed rows and inserts a new current version; IDENTITY keys are assigned in the INSERT's ORDER BY order, continuing from the table's highest value. Spark: Spark has no MERGE on DataFrames (Delta MERGE exists for tables); the job must compute the new state as a whole table from the previous state and the batch.
- TSQL-12 (construct) Cursors and WHILE loops. Legacy: A cursor processes rows one at a time in its ORDER BY order; variables carry state between rows (running totals, last values). NULL arithmetic inside the loop propagates: SET @total = @total + NULL makes @total NULL for the rest of the loop. Spark: Spark is set-based; loops become aggregations or ordered windows.
- TSQL-13 (construct) Temp tables. Legacy: #temp tables hold intermediate results for the session. Spark: Intermediate results are DataFrames or temporary views.
- TSQL-14 (semantic) LIKE character classes. Legacy: T-SQL LIKE supports character classes: '[0-9]' matches one digit, '[A-Z]' one letter (case-insensitively under a CI collation), '[^0-9]' a non-digit; % and _ as usual. Spark: Spark's LIKE has only % and _; '[0-9]' matches the literal text '[0-9]'.
- TSQL-15 (semantic) LEN ignores trailing spaces; SUBSTRING from 0; LEFT and RIGHT. Legacy: LEN(x) does not count trailing spaces (DATALENGTH does). SUBSTRING(x, 0, n) returns n-1 characters, because position 0 is before the string. LEFT/RIGHT count characters. Spark: length() counts trailing spaces; substring(x, 0, n) is treated like position 1 and returns n characters.
- TSQL-16 (semantic) CONVERT style codes. Legacy: CONVERT(type, date, style) formats dates by style: 101 mm/dd/yyyy, 103 dd/mm/yyyy, 104 dd.mm.yyyy, 105 dd-mm-yyyy, 106 dd mon yyyy, 111 yyyy/mm/dd, 112 yyyymmdd, 120 yyyy-mm-dd hh:mi:ss, 121 with milliseconds, 23 yyyy-mm-dd. Converting into a shorter CHAR(n)/VARCHAR(n) silently keeps the first n characters: CONVERT(CHAR(6), d, 112) is yyyymm. Spark: A cast to string gives yyyy-MM-dd; date_format needs a Java pattern; nothing truncates.
- TSQL-17 (construct) PIVOT. Legacy: PIVOT (aggregate(value) FOR col IN ([a], [b])) groups by every other column of the source and turns listed values into columns; values not listed are dropped; missing combinations give NULL. Spark: groupBy(...).pivot(col, values).agg(...) does the same when the values are listed; the grouping columns must be stated explicitly.
- TSQL-18 (semantic) EOMONTH and DATEADD at month-end. Legacy: DATEADD(month, n, d) clamps to the last day of the target month: DATEADD(month, 1, '2024-01-31') = '2024-02-29'; adding months to an earlier date never moves to a month-end. EOMONTH(d, n) returns the last day of the month n months away. Spark: add_months clamps the same way but also moves a last-day-of-month input to the target month's last day (add_months('2024-02-29', 1) = '2024-03-31'); last_day(d) is EOMONTH.
- TSQL-19 (semantic) Text ordering under collations (accents, case) in ORDER BY, MIN, MAX and rankings. Legacy: Under SQL_Latin1_General_CP1_CI_AS, text sorts case-insensitively with accent rules (Á sorts with A); MIN/MAX on text and ORDER BY text in a ranking follow that order. Spark: Spark sorts strings by code point: 'Zoe' < 'aoife' and 'Á' sorts after 'Z'.

findings.note: These lines drop the #customer_versions and #customer temp tables if they exist. In Spark they become DataFrames, so this code goes away.
The #customer_versions temp table holds the filtered CRM versions with version_count. In Spark it becomes an intermediate DataFrame.
The #customer temp table holds one chosen version per customer. In Spark it becomes an intermediate DataFrame.

full_name is built with + from first_name and last_name. If either is NULL, the legacy result is NULL. The translation must use concat(), which also returns NULL, not concat_ws(), which skips NULLs. The trap is latent if the source names are never NULL.
SUBSTRING(x, 0, 2) returns only 1 character in T-SQL, so initials are 2 letters. Spark's substring(x, 0, 2) returns 2 characters, which gives 4-letter initials.
The initials are joined with +, so a NULL first or last name makes them NULL. The translation must keep that NULL result.
PARTITION BY on the VARCHAR email column groups case variants together under the CI collation, so 'A@x.ie' and 'a@x.ie' count as one shared email. Spark keeps them apart.
PARTITION BY email also ignores trailing spaces, so 'a@x.ie ' and 'a@x.ie' land in the same partition in SQL Server but not in Spark.
DATEDIFF(YEAR, ...) counts year boundaries crossed, not full years elapsed. age_at_join must be year(customer_since) - year(date_of_birth), not floor(months_between/12).
The VARCHAR county is matched with IN against title-case names. SQL Server matches case variants such as 'DUBLIN', but Spark sends them to UNKNOWN.
The county IN check ignores trailing spaces in SQL Server ('Dublin ' matches). Spark does not.
The SOUTH county IN list matches case-insensitively in the legacy engine.
The SOUTH county IN list ignores trailing spaces in the legacy engine.
The WEST county IN list matches case-insensitively in the legacy engine.
The WEST county IN list ignores trailing spaces in the legacy engine.
The NORTH-WEST county IN list matches case-insensitively in the legacy engine.
The NORTH-WEST county IN list ignores trailing spaces in the legacy engine.
The MIDLANDS county IN list matches case-insensitively in the legacy engine.
The MIDLANDS county IN list ignores trailing spaces in the legacy engine.
LEN(eircode) ignores trailing spaces, so 'D02X285 ' still counts as 7 characters. Spark's length() counts 8 and marks the code invalid.
LEN(eircode) = 8 ignores trailing spaces. The translation needs rtrim before length() to give the same result.
segment_code is CHAR(4), so it holds 'STD ' padded with a space. SQL Server's = 'STD' ignores the padding, but Spark compares the padded value exactly and gets no match.
segment_code = 'STD' also matches 'std' or 'Std' under the CI collation. Spark's comparison is case-sensitive.
The output segment_code is CHAR(4), so legacy values come back padded to 4 characters. Spark output must keep or add that padding to match exactly.
